title: Cilostazol (Pletal)
mechanism: PDE3 inhibition → raised cAMP in platelets and vessels: antiplatelet and vasodilator

uses.agent: Cilostazol — added to aspirin or clopidogrel, symptomatic intracranial stenosis 50–99%
uses.doseText: 100 mg BID, 30 min before or 2 h after breakfast and dinner
notes: Label indication is claudication — stroke use is off-label in the US

renalHepatic: No renal adjustment; not removed by dialysis (95–98% protein bound) (label)

holdBeforeProcedure: Not stated in label — local policy
thrombolysisRule: Prior SAPT/DAPT doesn't exclude IVT — give if otherwise eligible (AHA 2026 §4.6.1 Rec 9: COR 1, B-NR); sICH +0.9% SAPT / +1.2% DAPT absolute (class-level statement; agent not named)

monitoring: Platelets and WBC — rare thrombocytopenia/leukopenia progressing to agranulocytosis (label)
interactions: Reduce to 50 mg BID with CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin, diltiazem) or CYP2C19 inhibitors (ticlopidine, fluconazole, omeprazole) (label)
pearls: Boxed warning: contraindicated in heart failure of any severity (label)
sources: Kleindorfer DO, et al. 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2021;52:e364-e467. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000375
